svg.title: During a vaginal examination of a laboring client, the nurse feels a pulsating loop of umbilical cord below the presenting part. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
svg.desc: Cord prolapse is a moment to act, not investigate: call for help with the emergency bell, lift the presenting part off the cord , position knee-chest or Trendelenburg, give oxygen, stop oxytocin, and prepare for immediate cesarean. Replacing the cord and leaving the client to go and call both feel helpful but are explicitly wrong.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Labor & Birth
Read the situation
During a vaginal examination of a laboring
client, the nurse feels a pulsating loop
of umbilical cord below the presenting
part. Which actions should the nurse take?
Select all that apply.
What fits here
Use a gloved hand to lift the presenting
part off the cord · Place the client in a
knee-chest or Trendelenburg position ·
Give oxygen, stop the oxytocin, and
prepare for immediate cesarean…
Why it fits
Cord prolapse is a moment to act, not
investigate: call for help with the
emergency bell, lift the presenting part
off the cord , position knee-chest or
Trendelenburg, give oxygen, stop oxytocin,
and prepare for immediate cesarean.
